title: [cupertino_ui] OverlayVisibilityMode.editing and .notEditing ignore focus
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

cupertino_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  cupertino_ui:
    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: cupertino_ui
      sha256: a47c4e7c66fd7444a063a602597fceb238f705c3f6b1322bc0053d0a2638ee6e
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.1.4"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample on iOS.
2. Type into the first field, then tap the second.

### Expected results

The first field's clear button goes away once you leave it, like UIKit's [`.whileEditing`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uitextfield/viewmode/whileediting).

### Actual results

It stays. `_shouldShowAttachment` in `text_field.dart` only checks for text (`editing => hasText`, `notEditing => !hasText`) and never looks at focus. Main has the same code, and the enum's docs describe it that way too, but the UIKit modes these mirror follow focus.

So `notEditing` disagrees with UIKit's [`.unlessEditing`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uitextfield/viewmode/unlessediting) in 3 of 4 cases, and `always` puts an X on an empty field, which UIKit never does.

| Does the X show? | `editing` | UIKit `.whileEditing` | `notEditing` | UIKit `.unlessEditing` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, not focused | no | no | yes | no |
| Empty, focused | no | no | yes | no |
| Text, not focused | yes | no | no | yes |
| Text, focused | yes | yes | no | no |

<details><summary>prefixMode and suffixMode</summary>

Same rule here. UIKit's `leftViewMode` and `rightViewMode` follow focus too, with one twist: `.unlessEditing` keeps the view on a focused field until there's text in it.

| Does the view show? | `editing` | UIKit `.whileEditing` | `notEditing` | UIKit `.unlessEditing` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, not focused | no | no | yes | yes |
| Empty, focused | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Text, not focused | yes | no | no | yes |
| Text, focused | yes | yes | no | no |

</details>

I checked UIKit on the iOS 26.2 simulator and cupertino_ui in a widget test.

void main() => runApp(

          children: [
            CupertinoTextField(clearButtonMode: OverlayVisibilityMode.editing),
            CupertinoTextField(placeholder: 'Tap here to leave the first field'),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    ),
  ),
);

title: [Android] TextField context menu does not show on long press after focus returns with an unchanged selection
EditableText does not update RenderEditable.hasFocus or its semantics isFocused when it regains focus with a valid selection
SpellCheckConfiguration == and hashCode ignore misspelledSelectionColor
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```dart
const red = SpellCheckConfiguration(misspelledSelectionColor: Color(0xFFFF0000));
const blue = SpellCheckConfiguration(misspelledSelectionColor: Color(0xFF0000FF));
print(red == blue); // true
```

Then rebuild an `EditableText` whose `spellCheckConfiguration` differs only in `misspelledSelectionColor` (same service and text style).

### Expected results

`red == blue` is `false`, and `EditableText` uses the new `misspelledSelectionColor`.

### Actual results

`SpellCheckConfiguration.operator ==` and `hashCode` don't include `misspelledSelectionColor` (added in #125162), so the two configurations compare equal. `EditableTextState.didUpdateWidget` only re-infers `_spellCheckConfiguration` when `oldWidget.spellCheckConfiguration != widget.spellCheckConfiguration`, so it keeps using the old selection color for misspelled words.

### Flutter version

`master` and stable 3.47.8.

title: Android platform views receive inconsistent pointer ids when a pointer lifts and another lands in the same frame
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Flutter app with a full-screen `AndroidView` (an `EagerGestureRecognizer` is set, so every pointer is forwarded).
2. In the native view, log every `MotionEvent` with its pointer ids, and flag events that are impossible given the earlier ones (e.g. `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down).
3. On a physical device, keep one finger down and repeatedly lift one finger while landing another at nearly the same moment (a "drumming" motion with 2–3 extra fingers).

In our test, 3 out of 8 such gestures produced an invalid stream within ~30 seconds.

### Expected results

The platform view receives a consistent pointer stream, as it would when hosted natively: each pointer id goes down once, keeps its id until it goes up, and every `MOVE` contains exactly the pointers that are down.

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(2)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]
```

### Actual results

The same finger is reported under different ids. The platform view receives `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down, `ACTION_POINTER_UP` for an id that never went down, and `MOVE` events whose pointer set changes without any down/up event:

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(2) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638   <- id 2 is already down
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688   <- lifts id 1, but the finger that lifted is id 2
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]                  <- id 2 disappears, id 1 stays
```

Native gesture code that tracks pointers by id breaks on this stream. For example, [mapbox-gestures-android](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gestures-android) throws `IllegalArgumentException: invalid pointerIndex -1` and `NullPointerException` ([mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter#1146](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter/issues/1146)), and those exceptions reach Dart as unhandled `PlatformException`s from `AndroidViewController.sendMotionEvent`.

#### Cause

Two id assignments are mixed in the stream the platform view receives:

1. **Dart assigns its own Android pointer ids.** `_AndroidMotionEventConverter.handlePointerDownEvent` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/platform_views.dart`) gives each new pointer the lowest id that is not in `usedAndroidPointerIds`, and frees an id as soon as it handles the pointer up. Android keeps the id of a lifted pointer reserved until the end of the input frame in which it lifted. So when a finger lifts and another lands in the **same frame**, Android gives the new finger a fresh id (2), but Dart reuses the id it just freed (1). From then on, Dart's ids and Android's ids for the same finger differ.

2. **The engine sends a mix of original and rebuilt events.** `PlatformViewsController.toMotionEvent` returns the original Android `MotionEvent` (with Android's ids) when its pointer count and action match the framework's event. Otherwise it rebuilds the event from the framework's pointer properties (with Dart's ids). This was added in #178528 (the fix for #176574). The check compares only the pointer count and action, not the pointer ids.

When the ids have diverged, `MOVE` events usually match and pass through with Android's ids. `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` events often don't, because Dart orders pointers by insertion and Android orders them by id, so the action index differs. Those events are rebuilt with Dart's ids. The platform view gets both kinds of event, so a finger's id appears to change.

Framework-side trace of the same moment (debug prints added locally to `_AndroidMotionEventConverter`; `androidId` is decoded from `event.device`):

```console
free   pointer=18 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                                t=15800488
assign pointer=19 androidId=2 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                    t=15800488  <- same frame: Android picks 2, Dart reuses 1
...
assign pointer=20 androidId=1 dartId=2 used={0, 1, 2}                t=15800638  <- Android reuses 1, Dart picks 2
send   _TransformedPointerDownEvent action=517 dartIds=[0, 1, 2]                  <- action index differs, so the engine rebuilds it with Dart's ids
```

Possible fixes: have `_AndroidMotionEventConverter` use Android's pointer id (it is already available in `PointerEvent.device`) instead of assigning its own, or have `toMotionEvent` compare pointer ids as well before reusing the original event.

```kotlin
class TouchCheckerView(context: Context) : View(context) {
  private val downIds = mutableSetOf<Int>()

  override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    val ids = (0 until event.pointerCount).map { event.getPointerId(it) }
    val actionId = event.getPointerId(event.actionIndex)
    Log.d(TAG, "${MotionEvent.actionToString(event.action)} ids=$ids t=${event.eventTime}")

    val expected = when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds + actionId
      else -> downIds.toSet()
    }
    when {
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN && actionId in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_DOWN for id $actionId, which is already down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP && actionId !in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_UP for id $actionId, which is not down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked != MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL && ids.toSet() != expected ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: event has ids $ids, expected $expected")
    }

    when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> { downIds.clear(); downIds += actionId }
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds += actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP -> downIds -= actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> downIds.clear()
    }
    return true
  }
}

title: [web] iOS Safari: Japanese IME duplicates composed text in a TextField with enableInteractiveSelection: false
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the code sample below for the web and open it in Safari on iOS.
2. Add the Japanese Kana keyboard (Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard > Japanese > Kana) and switch to it with the globe key.
3. Tap the "selection off" field. On the 12-key Kana layout, tap は, tap な, then choose the candidate 花.
4. Do the same in the "default" field and in the "selection off, single-line" field.

Reproduced on the iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 27.0, Safari 27.0, with a debug web build on Flutter 3.47.7 stable. The same duplication also showed up in a Flutter web app that uses `enableInteractiveSelection: false`, on the iOS 18.6 Simulator (Safari 18.6) and on a real iPhone (iOS 18.7.1, Safari). Desktop Safari was not tested.

### Expected results

Every field composes in place, as the default field does: は, then はな, then 花.

### Actual results

The two "selection off" fields set `enableInteractiveSelection: false`.

| Field                              | after は | after な | after 花 |
|------------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| selection off (textarea)           | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |
| default (textarea)                 | は       | はな     | 花       |
| selection off, single-line (input) | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |

Each key after the first re-inserts the whole preedit at the caret, and choosing the candidate appends it instead of replacing the preedit. The field keeps the duplicated text: the hidden DOM element and the rendered field both end with ははな花.

---

**Cause**

On iOS Safari, `IOSTextEditingStrategy` routes the hidden element's `input` event and the document's `selectionchange` to `DefaultTextEditingStrategy.handleChange`, which first calls `suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`. When `enableInteractiveSelection` is false and the DOM selection is not collapsed, that function collapses the selection to its end and writes it back with `EditingState.applyToDomElement` (`value = text`, then `setSelectionRange`). The write happens synchronously inside the event, and nothing checks for an active composition.

WebKit dispatches each `insertCompositionText` input event while the selection spans the marked text (`[0,1]`, `[1,3]` and `[3,4]` in the log below). The engine collapses that selection during the event. After that, WebKit no longer treats the text as marked, but it never fires `compositionend`. The next key therefore starts a new composition at the caret with the whole preedit as its data, and the candidate arrives as one more composition inserted at the caret.

- 3.47.7: [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1617-L1642), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1644-L1660), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1065-L1079)
- main (aebd23e2d4): [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1800-L1825), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1827-L1843), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1191-L1205). The function is unchanged on main.

`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded` was added in #171935, which first shipped in 3.35.0. I have not bisected this.

**Suggested fix**

Skip the DOM write while a composition is active, but still return the collapsed state to the framework. This is the same approach as the existing guard in `updateElementPlacement`, which skips `placeElement()` while `composingText != null` (#98817, fixed by flutter/engine#51323; [3.47.7](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1541-L1555), [main](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1713-L1727)):

```dart
    final EditingState newEditingState = editingState.copyWith(
      baseOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
      extentOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
    );
    // Writing the DOM selection mid-composition makes WebKit drop the
    // composition without a compositionend. See also #98817.
    if (composingText == null) {
      newEditingState.applyToDomElement(activeDomElement);
    }
    return newEditingState;
```

`compositionupdate` sets `composingText` before the `input` event, so the check covers both the `input` and the `selectionchange` paths. `InputEvent.isComposing` would cover only `input`. I have not tested this patch.

This is related to #193847 (fixed by #194096) but is a different bug: that one is a stale composing range after the framework rewrites the text in the middle of a composition.

body:
**Once an app calls `setFlashMode`, every `takePicture()` sets the same flash mode on
`ImageCapture` again, which adds roughly 250-300 ms to each capture.** This happens
even when the mode is `FlashMode.off` and never changes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.high`.
2. Call `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)`.
3. Call `takePicture()` repeatedly and measure the latency.

### Results

| | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `setFlashMode` never called | 517 ms | 360 ms |
| `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)` called once | **794 ms** | **656 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart. "ZSL on" means
`setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.

### Why

`takePicture` calls `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` before every capture whenever a
flash mode has been set (since flutter/packages#3800). CameraX keeps the flash mode
on the `ImageCapture` instance for subsequent captures, so the repeated call does not
change anything. In CameraX 1.6.2, `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` has no check for an
unchanged mode, so each call still goes through `CameraControl.setFlashMode`. (The
androidx-main source has since added that check.)

### Proposed fix

Only call `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` in `takePicture` when the mode differs from the
one last applied to the current `ImageCapture` instance. The torch behavior from
flutter/packages#4903 (clearing a previous flash mode when torch is enabled) stays
the same.

title: [camera_android_camerax] Zero-shutter-lag has no effect with ResolutionPreset.max
body:
**With `ResolutionPreset.max`, zero-shutter-lag (ZSL) has no effect, so none of the
`ResolutionPreset`s gives full-resolution photos with ZSL.** The other presets work
with ZSL, but cap the photo size (`high`: 1280x720; `ultraHigh` requests 16:9 up to
3840x2160).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.max` on a device where
   `isZeroShutterLagSupported()` returns `true`.
2. Call `setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.
3. Measure `takePicture()` latency.

### Results

Every call succeeds and nothing is logged, but capture latency does not change:

| Preset | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `ResolutionPreset.high` | 517 ms | **360 ms** |
| `ResolutionPreset.max` | 828 ms | **826 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart.

### Why

**CameraX turns ZSL off when any bound use case prefers higher resolution over
capture rate, and `ResolutionPreset.max` sets that on every use case** (since
flutter/packages#11956).

This is not in the `ImageCapture` docs, which list only `VideoCapture`, flash and
extensions. In CameraX 1.6.2, `UseCase.mergeConfigs()` sets `OPTION_ZSL_DISABLED` on
any use case whose `ResolutionSelector` uses a non-default allowed resolution mode,
and ZSL is turned off if any bound use case has that flag.

### Proposed fix

- When ZSL is enabled, `ResolutionPreset.max` uses the largest regular size for still
  capture, that is, the largest size in the normal output size list rather than the
  separate high-resolution list (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`). Without ZSL, still
  capture with `max` is unchanged.
- `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` with `max` no longer prefer higher resolution, with
  or without ZSL (see below).

On the Galaxy S21 this gives full-resolution photos with ZSL: 3024x4032, with the
same latency as `high` + ZSL.

### Trade-off to confirm

On devices whose largest photo size is only in the high-resolution list, enabling
ZSL with `max` gives the largest regular size instead. For the device reported in
flutter/packages#11956 that would be 3264x2448 instead of 4624x3468. CameraX does not
allow ZSL with high-resolution sizes.

### Preview and ImageAnalysis

flutter/packages#11956 first applied the high-resolution mode to `ImageCapture` only,
since the original issue was about still capture. At review request it was extended
to `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis`, so that `max` means the highest resolution across
the board.

Keeping it there would keep ZSL off:

- `Preview` cannot be recreated when ZSL is enabled. Recreating it creates a new
  `SurfaceProducer` and so a new texture ID, but that ID was already returned as the
  camera ID, and the camera package only allows enabling ZSL after initialization.
- High-resolution sizes cannot sustain 20 fps (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`), which
  streaming use cases like `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` rely on.

On the Galaxy S21 the `max` preview is 1440x1080 with or without the mode. Is there a
use case that needs high-resolution sizes for `Preview` or `ImageAnalysis`?

title: [web] Safari 27 + minimum font size > 16: typography sentinel line-height factor still mismatches after #186474
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #185931 (fixed by #186474). The same symptom is still reproducible on **Safari 27.2** when Safari's minimum font size is set above 16 *before* the page loads.

The engine's typography sentinel ends up with a clamped `font-size` **and** a proportionally scaled `line-height`, so the expected line-height factor (`9999 / fontSize`) no longer equals the measured ratio (`lineHeight / fontSize`). The engine then treats line-height as overridden and applies a bogus `lineHeightScaleFactorOverride` (~625), which stretches every layout.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.44.8 (stable), engine `0cd610717b` (2026-07-23)
- Safari 27.2 (AppleWebKit 605.1.15), macOS
- Safari → Settings → Advanced → "Never use font sizes smaller than: **19**" (`WebKitMinimumFontSize = 19`), set before load
- `flutter build web --release`, default renderer (CanvasKit)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set "Never use font sizes smaller than" to a value greater than 16, quit and relaunch Safari.
2. Load an app route that lays out a scrollable content column.

## Expected

Normal layout (works in Chromium).

## Actual

The header renders, then remaining widgets are pushed thousands of pixels down inside an enormous scroll view — or the page appears blank. Zooming in/out forces a re-layout that sometimes paints correctly.

## Measurements

Reading the sentinel (`p` with text `flutter typography measurement`) via `getComputedStyle`:

**Broken (minimum font size 19):**

```
font-size:   16.52174px
line-height: 10325.05px
measured ratio:              10325.05 / 16.52174 = 625.0
engine expectation (current): 9999 / 16.52174     = 605.2   <-- mismatch
```

**With the sentinel forced above the clamp:**

```
font-size:   100px
line-height: 9999px
ratio:       99.990 = 9999 / 100   <-- matches, layout renders normally
```

Both values appear to be scaled by the same browser text-scale factor (1.0326 here), while `defaultLineHeightFactor` in `lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/platform_dispatcher.dart` still divides the *unscaled* `9999` by the *scaled* font size.

Effect of the fix on the same page: semantics nodes went from 4 (stretched) to 51, and exposed text from 16 chars (page header only) to 1511 chars (full content).

## Workaround

```css
p[aria-hidden="true"] { font-size: 100px !important; }
```

Placed in `index.html` so it applies before the engine creates/measures the sentinel. This keeps the sentinel above the clamp threshold, so neither value is scaled and the ratios match.

## Notes

- Firestore, CORS and WebGL were ruled out on the same machine: SDK reads return in ~0.5 s, REST reads in ~0.3 s, WebGL2 is available and the home route renders normally.
- Happy to provide a minimal repro app if the existing sample at https://alancook.github.io/patient-manager/safari-test/ is not sufficient.

title: [iOS][UIScene] Plugins receive application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: twice on a cold launch with connection options (background_fetch crashes)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Take an iOS app on Flutter 3.44.1 that has adopted the UIScene lifecycle (`UIApplicationSceneManifest` in Info.plist, `UISceneDelegateClassName` = `FlutterSceneDelegate` or a subclass; plugins registered from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine`).
2. Add a plugin that still uses the application lifecycle (no `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate`) and does something that must happen exactly once in `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`. The real-world case is `background_fetch` (Transistorsoft), which registers its `BGTaskScheduler` launch handler there. A minimal stand-in is a `FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate` that counts calls (see code sample).
3. Terminate the app.
4. Cold-launch it through something that carries **scene connection options**: tap a local/push notification, a Live Activity, a Home Screen quick action, or open a custom URL scheme (`xcrun simctl openurl <udid> myscheme://x` reproduces it on the simulator).

Launching from the app icon (no connection options) does not reproduce.

### Expected results

Plugins receive `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:` once per process, as they do under the classic app-delegate lifecycle.

### Actual results

Plugins receive it **twice** within the same launch:

1. From the storyboard `FlutterViewController` init: `sceneFallbackWillFinishLaunchingApplication:` / `sceneFallbackDidFinishLaunchingApplication:` ([FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324)). This sets `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch = YES` ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129)).
2. Again from `scene:willConnectToSession:options:` when no plugin claims the connection: `FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate` calls `sceneWillConnectFallback:` ([FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270)), which converts the connection options to launch options and calls `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:YES` directly, **without checking `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch`** ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173)). Its own guard (`_sceneWillConnectFallbackCalled`) only prevents a third call; it does not know about the first one.

The only difference between the two deliveries is the `launchOptions` dictionary (empty the first time, the converted connection options the second time), so a plugin cannot tell them apart.

With `background_fetch` the second call ends the process in under a second:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInternalInconsistencyException',
reason: 'Launch handler for task with identifier com.transistorsoft.fetch has already been registered'

-[BGTaskScheduler registerForTaskWithIdentifier:usingQueue:launchHandler:]
-[TSBackgroundFetch registerAppRefreshTask]
-[TSBackgroundFetch didFinishLaunching]
-[BackgroundFetchPlugin application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate sceneWillConnectFallback:]
-[FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:flutterEngine:options:]
-[FlutterSceneDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:options:]
```

Seen in production on iOS 18 through iOS 27 (same engine, so the OS version does not matter); 100% of launches from a Live Activity / notification tap crashed, while icon launches were fine, which is why it passed QA. The code paths above are unchanged on `master` at 7102630 as of 2026-10-27.

Workaround that works for us: register a tiny `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate` through `registrar.addSceneDelegate(...)` whose `scene(_:willConnectTo:options:)` returns `true`. Because a plugin then "handled" the connection, the engine skips `sceneWillConnectFallback:`. That is only acceptable when the app consumes its URL / notification / shortcut itself via the scene delegate; otherwise legacy plugins lose the launch options.

Suggested fix: make `sceneWillConnectFallback:` respect `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch` (or merge the two fallbacks so the converted connection options are passed in the single delivery). Related readability issue: #185705.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

A lifecycle delegate that shows the double delivery without any third-party plugin. Register it from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine` (so it exists before the storyboard `FlutterViewController` is created), then cold-launch via a URL scheme or notification tap.

```swift
final class LaunchCounter: NSObject, FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate {
  private var count = 0
  func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                   didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
    count += 1
    print("didFinishLaunching delivered \(count)x, options: \(launchOptions.keys)")
    precondition(count == 1, "didFinishLaunching delivered twice")   // trips on the second delivery
    return true
  }
}

// in AppDelegate (FlutterAppDelegate subclass, UIScene manifest present)
func didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine(_ engineBridge: FlutterImplicitEngineBridge) {
  GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: engineBridge.pluginRegistry)
  engineBridge.pluginRegistry.registrar(forPlugin: "LaunchCounter")?
    .addApplicationDelegate(LaunchCounter())
}
```

Output on a tap/URL cold launch:

```
didFinishLaunching delivered 1x, options: []
didFinishLaunching delivered 2x, options: [UIApplicationLaunchOptionsKey(_rawValue: UIApplicationLaunchOptionsURLKey), ...]
```

</details>

title: [material_ui] Radio and Checkbox put cupertino_ui's radio and checkbox in every Android build
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

material_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  cupertino_ui:
    dependency: transitive
    description:
      name: cupertino_ui
      sha256: a47c4e7c66fd7444a063a602597fceb238f705c3f6b1322bc0053d0a2638ee6e
      url: "https://pub.dev"

  material_ui:
    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: material_ui
      sha256: e4031746f96c8316864d9b92bce375f1320a36ed56e166307e1e1bda9d90b4ab
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.8.0"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter build apk --release --analyze-size --target-platform=android-arm64` with the code sample.
2. Look for `cupertino_ui/src/radio.dart` and `src/checkbox.dart` in the report.

### Expected results

Neither file, since only `Radio.adaptive` and `Checkbox.adaptive` build Cupertino controls.

### Actual results

| Build | `radio.dart` | `checkbox.dart` |
|---|---|---|
| Code sample | 8,728 B | 9,355 B |
| Without the `Radio` and `Checkbox` | none | none |

`build` picks the `.adaptive` arm from a private field (`_radioType`, `_checkboxType`), so AOT keeps it. `RadioListTile` and `CheckboxListTile` do the same.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: _Controls())));

class _Controls extends StatelessWidget {
  const _Controls();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => RadioGroup<int>(
    groupValue: 1,
    onChanged: (_) {},
    child: Column(
      children: [
        const Radio<int>(value: 1),
        Checkbox(value: true, onChanged: (_) {}),
      ],
    ),
  );
}
```

</details>
